quest.title: Liyue Celebrates and Eight Adepts Face a Hidden Calamity
quest.description: The Lantern Rite has come around once more. What stories will be written in Liyue Harbor this year...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6, Recipe: Drunken Plums in Snow x1, Unknown Item #373194 x1

chapter.title: Liyue Celebrates and Eight Adepts Face a Hidden Calamity

talks.objective: Take a stroll around Liyue Harbor

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, it's Hu Tao!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, she looks kinda troubled... Shall we go say hi?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there, Heroes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the...!? Oh, Xiangling!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hehe, I was just kidding around. Happy Lantern Rite! Hope I didn't scare ya?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nah, of course not! We were just about to go say hi to Hu Tao.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I noticed — which is why I stopped you! We can't disturb her now, or we won't get to see the brand-spanking-new Director Hu.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean by that?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Well, I gave her a new outfit as a gift, but she's so used to her uniform that she's hesitant to try it on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! What kind of outfit is it?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: A bright red one, of course! The color of prosperity, and the color of Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: But just so you're aware... Hu Tao's not really been herself lately. Whenever I invite her to hang out, she either finds an excuse not to come, or spends the whole time staring into space.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I've tried asking her what's wrong, but she won't even admit there's a problem. *sigh*... Anyway, so that outfit was my way of saying that I'm here as her friend, and I hope she'll feel better soon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon was just thinking that she looked kinda troubled...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: But you've never seen Hu Tao like this before. What could it possibly be?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Just then, you feel something cool against your face... Someone has crept up behind you and is now covering your eyes.
Guess whooo~?

choices.text: I recognize those dulcet tones anywhere, Zhongli.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #Oh, I see... So our consultant is the one you miss most. You're breaking my heart, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I was just kidding. Happy Lantern Rite!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hee-hee, Happy Lantern Rite!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Hu Tao, is that a new outfit? It looks great!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: All thanks to Xiangling! Apparently, it was custom made by a designer from Fontaine... I hope it didn't put you out too much?

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Nope! The tailor happened to be in Liyue looking for a change of scenery and fresh inspiration. We got talking and really hit it off. So it was no trouble at all!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Well that's good. Thanks again Xiangling, you have exquisite taste!

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Oh, stop. I'm just glad you like it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, Hu Tao. What's been bothering you?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Huh? Why would you ask that? ...Is it my tone of voice? Not as sweet and melodious as you're used to?

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Your voice is as sweet as ever Hu Tao, but we're your friends. You can't hide how you're feeling from us, no matter how hard you may try.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Haha, alright, alright. I wasn't trying to hide anything from you, I promise. It's just, I've been struggling with a... work-related thing.

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Work-related? You mean the funeral parlor?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Uh-huh. So, you see? It's a part of my duty as the Director. Besides, it's Lantern Rite. I don't want you worrying about me when you're supposed to be enjoying the festival!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: So relax. Everything will be A-OK, 'cause Director Hu will find a way!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You, stressing about work? That's gotta be a first. Guess it must be something super complicated, huh?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Yup, it's a doozy! I feel like I've been banging my head against a brick wall.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go get Keqing, she'll know what to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You think Keqing will be able to help?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She can at least teach Hu Tao about work-life balance.

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Good idea! Especially since it's festival season. I heard the Ministry of Civil Affairs is putting on a street fair with loads of cool stuff to do.

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Forget about work for now, Hu Tao. Come have fun with us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Take some time to relax and recover your energy, then you'll knock this thing out in no time!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Ah, I'd love to, but I'm afraid I have a meeting to get to... A real meeting, I'm not just making excuses!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, really? You sure you can't get out of it?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: ...How about this, you guys go on ahead, and I'll meet you at the fair when I'm done. Sound good?

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Hmm... Okay, fair enough. But don't take too long! And after the fair, how about we all have a meal at Wanmin Restaurant? My treat, of course.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Count me in! I could never turn down Xiangling's cooking.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hee-hee, me neither! Paimon's drooling already...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like a plan. Hope your meeting goes well, Hu Tao!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Don't worry about me! Get yourselves to the fair, I'll join you as soon as I can.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Ah, wonderful, you still remember my voice. That means, you must have missed me a lot...

talks.objective: Check out the Lantern Rite street fair

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: This is the Custom Gift Envelope stall. You can pick your preferred design, leave a custom message, and hand them out to friends and family.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: If you're interested, Madame Lan Yan, please take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I take it these coins go inside the envelope? They look a little different from regular Mora...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: That's right. These are special-edition Fortune Coins issued by the Coinage Office. There are twelve designs in total, each engraved with motifs from the Guyan Sigils that represent different blessings.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Take this one, for example. This design is—

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: The Sign of Vaisravana! Yes, originally an exorcism sigil widely used in thaumaturgy. These days, it's used as a lucky charm to prevent disaster and bring favor. Quite popular with business owners hoping for peace and prosperity...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: ...Ah! I interrupted you, didn't I? Sorry, I just got a little carried away... I meant no offense, Lady Yuheng.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Hehe, none taken, Madame Lan.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Really, it's my honor to meet a member of the historic Lan lineage. Your ancestors hailed from the Twelve Tribes of Chenyu Vale, and were renowned for their proficiency in the mystic arts.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: You flatter me, Lady Yuheng! My family are but distant relatives. We would hardly consider ourselves the true heirs to that illustrious lineage.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: There's no need to be humble. Your knowledge of the Guyan Sigils is very impressive. A rare find in the Liyue Harbor of today.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: True heir or not, you do your ancestors proud. And given your level of erudition in this area, I may find myself requesting your help in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Hehe, well, I won't deny that I pride myself in my level of learning... So by all means, it would be my pleasure to assist the Lady Yuheng.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Keqing! Hard at work with the festivities as usual, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME} and Paimon! And Xiangling, too. I was just thinking about you this morning, wondering if I'd get to see you during the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I hope you're keeping a reasonable work-life balance this year?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Haha, oh, don't even go there... The Ministry of Civil Affairs has had so much to do this Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Oh, before I forget — everyone, this is Madame Lan Yan, a master craftswoman from the Chenyu Vale Artisans Association.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: She kindly agreed to help the Ministry of Civil Affairs with this year's street fair. In a short while, you'll get to see her work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Nice to meet you, Madame Lan!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Madame Lan, allow me to introduce—

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, {M#his}{F#her} travel buddy Paimon, and Xiangling! Hello!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Haha, it seems like you're getting carried away again, Madame Lan...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Ah! Sorry, interrupted again, didn't I... Hehe, it's just quite exciting, meeting these three people I've heard so much about. I never imagined I'd get the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I think you mean two people, right? I'm just a chef — a good one, but it's not THAT much to get excited about. You don't need to include me just to be polite.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Oh, I beg to differ! The first meal I ate in Liyue Harbor was at Wanmin Restaurant. Xiangling's cooking gave my tastebuds plenty to be excited about!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello, Madame Lan. Nice to meet a master craftswoman.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Please, call me Lan Yan. And I'm no "master craftswoman," just a humble maker of handicrafts.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I'm sure anyone who's seen your work would disagree. Speaking of which, I'm sure you'd all like to see it — why don't you come with me, and I'll show you?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Here it is. This is a game for the street fair, where you duel with rattan figures. It's called "Immortal Combat."

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: There are eight rattan figures in total, and thanks to some ingenious design work, they can move around on their own. Madame Lan took inspiration from the legend of the Eight Adepts. Astonishing, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds amazing! But what are the Eight Adepts? Are they like, adepti?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: They're not actual adepti, but eight legendary people said to have had adeptus-like abilities — which earned them the title of the Eight Adepts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Paimon's never heard that story before...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: They were only around for a short time, and it was two or three thousand years ago. So their stories aren't nearly as well-known as those of the actual adepti.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Also, did you notice this year's Mingxiao Lantern when you arrived in the harbor?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shaped like a huge tree, right?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Yes. It's said that during the Archon War period, there was a divine mountain in Liyue with a giant tree on its summit. A tree who was also a god, named "Tao Dou."

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Oh! I think I heard that one from a storyteller once — "The Sanctification of Tao Dou." So Tao Dou is the giant tree...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And this tree was also a god?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Correct. Back then, people thought that behind Tao Dou was the realm of the dead, and if you committed grave sins in life, your soul would be unable to pass beyond that tree and into the afterlife.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Even today, in my hometown people still say things like, "You'll never cross Mt. Tao Dou when you die." It's very insulting though, so don't go around repeating it...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: When the Archon War arrived, Tao Dou was dragged into the fighting, disturbing the realm of the dead. The boundary between life and death became blurred, and death began to encroach on the realm of the living.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... and then what?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: That's where The Sanctification of Tao Dou comes in! The Eight Adepts rose up to solve the crisis, and laid down a great magic array to purify Tao Dou.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Exactly. After that, Tao Dou's remains sank into the Ley Lines and became a border, separating the living of Liyue from the dead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, THE border? The border between life and death? That's where it comes from?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: So the legends say, but who knows if it's true.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those Eight Adepts must be super powerful if they could purify a god... Are we sure they weren't just adepti?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Yep — and in fact, their tale specifically emphasizes that most of them were ordinary humans!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: If I remember right, they were from several groups that joined forces... a Guizang one, a Lianshan one, and...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Right! The Three Hermits of Guizang, the Two Sages of Lianshan, and the Three Beasts of Tao Dou. Collectively, the Eight Adepts. The mainstream narrative holds that the Guizang Hermits and the Lianshan Sages were human.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I know one of the hermits was "Wind Reader," said to be the founder of the ancient art of Qimen Divination.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: If I'm not mistaken, he hailed from the Twelve Tribes of Chenyu Vale. His descendants became the Lan clan, and kept the art of Qimen Divination alive. Madame Lan, correct me if I'm wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: That's certainly what the clan genealogies claim, although my personal knowledge of Qimen Divination is very patchy.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: The second hermit's story is somewhat more amusing. He mastered the art of fishing with a rod and line, and became known to the people as the "Yunlai Angler."

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: You may have heard of Yunlai Swordsmanship, which is the style I trained in. Both that style and its more ancient variant have their origins in the Yunlai Angler's rod-wielding techniques...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Seriously? ...Haha, did Xingqiu tell you that? 'Cause it sounds like something right out of a martial arts novel!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what about the third hermit?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: That would be the Wuwang Kid... also known as Old Man Wuwang. The story goes that he always presented himself in child form. As a hermit, his expertise lay with Qihuang sigils, which he used to catch demons, heal disease, and protect lives from the encroaching presence of death.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor should be best acquainted with his story, since their founders were said to have studied under the Wuwang Kid.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: They were just ordinary people like you and me. But when faced with mounting disasters, they used what strength they had to guard the border between life and death. Fortunately, they were aided by their knowledge of a secret art, which the funeral parlor still practices to this day.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: So it's true? The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor really does have a secret art?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I heard from Hu Tao that she has a flaming staff handed down by her forebearers. Apparently, it has special powers, used for cleansing rituals...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: But it could just be another one of her tall tales. ...Oh, you probably haven't met Hu Tao yet, have you? She's the director at the funeral parlor.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I've never had the pleasure, but I've certainly heard of Director Hu Tao.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, well these Guizang Hermits sound pretty legit. How about the two sages and the three beasts? What's their story?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: One was Sage Hu, a master of gourd crafts, and the other was Sage Jian, an expert in bronze mirrors.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Very little information survives on these two. All we know is that they practiced the secret art of Lianshan, earning them the title of the Two Sages of Lianshan.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I heard there's a hidden palace deep in the mountains south of Stone Gate. Traditionally, that's believed to be where they retreated for cultivation.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: As for the three beasts, their retreat was Mt. Tao Dou, hence the "Three Beasts of Tao Dou." As their title suggests, those three were not humans.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what were they? Monsters or something...?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: They were... Ganyu?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh? All three of them?

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, right! Ganyu's here, okay!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite, Ganyu.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... I hope I'm not interrupting anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course not!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: What is it? Ningguang's back?

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Yes. The others have arrived, too.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Got it, thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: My apologies, everyone, but I've got to go. Ganyu and I have some important work to attend to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, what? Not you, too... seems like everyone's busy with work.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: You know what it's like — the festival season is upon us, so it's all systems go at the Ministry of Civil Affairs. Don't worry, everything's fine.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Yes, you should focus on enjoying everything that the street fair has to offer. And if you find anything is not to your satisfaction, we will welcome your feedback.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Bye for now, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: One second, Ganyu...

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: #What is it, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Don't forget to take breaks. Look after yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: #Haha, {NICKNAME}'s being especially nice today, checking in on everyone's wellbeing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, what other option does {F#s}he have? It's not like {F#s}he can drag them away from their desks and force them to have fun against their will.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Thanks for your concern, we'll be sure to take care... and I hope you'll do the same.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I actually have something I need to do as well, so I should get to the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Oh, are you looking for Hu Tao? She's supposed to meet us here so we can grab lunch. Why don't you come with? If you don't mind the extra company, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Not at all, I'd love to! What a nice surprise!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Perfect! Hmm, Hu Tao should have joined us here by now... I guess her meeting overran. Why don't we head to the funeral parlor?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Earlier, just outside the funeral parlor...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: ...So in other words, Butler An, you'd like to go without the drums?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Exactly. Since this has come at such a festive time, I'd rather keep things low-key to avoid disturbing the celebrations.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Understood. What about paper effigies for burning? We can do mansions, chariots, boats, or sedan chairs...

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Sure, but let's stick with something small. His Lordship has never been a fan of ostentation.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: In that case... how about an effigy of a silk gown? Something to please the family, but not too over-the-top. Does that sound alright?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: It sounds perfect. You think of everything, Director Hu.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Great. And will you be providing your own cinerary casket?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Yes, His Lordship had one made two years ago, in fact. He sourced an excellent block of gloomwood, and had an artisan convert it into a casket. It's currently being stored at the old family house at Yilong Wharf.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Gloomwood is a good choice. Flame-resistant, water-resistant, and insect-resistant. Now, what about the mourning tent and the procession? Did the family say what style they want?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: We can certainly keep them simple, but I wouldn't recommend foregoing them entirely. You don't want the public speculating about why the Feiyun Commerce Guild couldn't seem to afford a proper funeral.

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: It's like you read my mind — Master expressed the same concern. But he also said he has full confidence in the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's judgment in this area.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Very well. Then my suggestion for the tent would be sloped rooves — one with a ridged spine, two of them curved at the top. Thirty-six seats, no more, no less, and all with fresh silk covers. But not just any silk — they should be decorated with the Feiyun symbols.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: At the front, we want a moon gate, a Grand Preceptor armchair, and bamboo railings. Sufficiently grand, but tasteful and measured. Would this be suitable, Butler An?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: That sounds ideal. Oh, and we should put some rugs down. Make them tortoise-shell, His Lordship is very fond of that color.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: That can be arranged. How about the procession?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Master requested no music procession, but sixteen pallbearers. Nothing flashy — plain clothes will do, as long as they're smart and all dressed the same.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: And the carriage?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Open sedan chair please, with four pairs of white plaques and twenty pairs of red plaques.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Any ceremonial weaponry and such?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Yes, two sets of gold weaponry and two sets of soul banners, four items per set.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Okay, for the gold weaponry, a four-piece set would be the mace, battle axe, stirrup, and fist, so two each of those. And then we could do two clear passage banners, plus two each of the Flying Tiger, Flying Carp, and Flying Turtle banners.

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: That will do nicely.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Alright, last thing: How about the hanging banner and the portrait pavilion?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: For the hanging banner, we want an octagonal tube with eight tassels per corner, and a dome of red gauze covering the top. As for the portrait pavilion, we're looking to do one incense pavilion with two spare rooms — one as a changing room, the other as a display room. And we'd like a plain white cover over the whole thing.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Did you want that embroidered?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Ah, I knew I missed something... The family neglected to consider that in their sorrow. But it's a minor detail. What would your suggestion be?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Well, the Feiyun Commerce Guild is a large and prosperous family with four generations living under one roof. As the founder of this family, His Lordship could not be more blessed.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Added to that, he has reached a ripe old age, lived a virtuous life, and is spending his final days in peace and comfort. All in all, he has lived a very complete life.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: In which case, I'd recommend embroidering a bats-of-longevity motif and a cranes-and-deer-of-youth motif, to pass on his good fortune to the next generation.

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Excellent! I must say, Director Hu, you really understand your clients.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Of course, think nothing of it... Huh? Ah, Ms. Baiwen.

dialogues.speaker: Baiwen
dialogues.text: Greetings, Director Hu. Lady Ningguang has arrived, and she would be most grateful if you could join her at Yujing Terrace.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Wow, that was quick. Alright, I'll head over in two ticks.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Butler An, my sincere apologies, but I'm afraid I have another meeting to get to.

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Of course, I've taken plenty of your time already. Don't let me keep you.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Ferry, can I leave you to follow up on the Feiyun funeral arrangements?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Of course, Director. I'll handle it.

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: The Hu family is truly blessed. It seems their directors go from strength to strength with each generation.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: I agree. She was born for the job.

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Ah yes — Madame Undertaker, I didn't get the chance to discuss payment with the director.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: There's no rush. I gathered from your conversation that the situation is still unfolding. This was just an initial meeting so that we can make advance preparations, yes?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: That's right. Master asked me to come a few days ahead of time so that things aren't rushed at the last minute. On that note, please do keep everything strictly confidential for now. No public announcements.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Of course. You have my word.

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Thanks. Could I trouble you for a pro forma invoice? Easier for the family to review that way.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: I'll get that to you in due course... Hello, can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hey, Ferry. We're looking for Hu Tao, is she here?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: You just missed her, unfortunately. She's attending a meeting elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Oh... Any idea when she'll be back?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: She didn't say, but she only left a moment ago. She could be some time.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: If it's anything urgent, I'd be happy to take a message for you, and I'll relay it to her as soon as she returns.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Oh... No, it's nothing urgent...

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: If you'd prefer to speak with her directly, you can always wait till she's free.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well this sucks. Paimon thought Hu Tao would be done with work by now.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I guess she's got more on her plate than we realized... Well, there's not much point in hanging around here. Why don't we go eat and come back later?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon is getting a little hungry, but shouldn't we wait for Hu Tao?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: It sounded like she's gonna be a while. Besides, I can always fire up the stove again once she's back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, sounds good! Madame Lan, you must be getting hungry too, right? You should come with us!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Madame Lan...?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Oh! Sorry, I spaced out... Whatever works for you.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Alright Ferry, we'll head off then. Can you let Hu Tao know where we are when she gets back?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Sure. Take care, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Butler An?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Ma'am, do you happen to know who that young lady with the black hair is?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: I haven't met her before, but that silver swallow hairpiece makes me wonder if she's from Chenyu Vale.

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Chenyu Vale, hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Something the matter?

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Well, it's just... So, the other day when I was out shopping, I ran into her and Master. They were chatting away, and I noticed that she showed him a very peculiar-looking rattan figure.

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Later that day, as I was moving His Lordship to a more comfortable bedroom, I saw something underneath his bed... and would you know it, it was that same rattan figure!

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: There was some kind of spell written on it. It was icy-cold to the touch, and made the whole room chilly... The whole thing seems very sinister.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Oh my goodness... Are you suggesting that there could be unnatural causes behind His Lordship's condition?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Well, I've heard they practice Qimen magic in Chenyu Vale. Pentad Fortune Conveyance, Fate Transference, and the like...

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: The last thing I want to do is start suspecting anyone, but... with His Lordship bedridden, and Master urging me to start discussing funeral arrangements, I can't help but think...

dialogues.speaker: An Su
dialogues.text: Ahem! Sorry, look at me rambling away... I'm sure I'm just being paranoid... Please forget I said anything, and certainly don't repeat this to anyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Butler An. The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor understands the importance of discretion. Client confidentiality is paramount.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Dad, I brought some friends over! I'm cooking today! ...Hmm? Dad? Daaad...

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: Over here, Xiangling!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, there he is! He's over at Ying'er's place. Let's go say hi.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Timaeus!? What's wrong with him?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Hmm, that scent...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Ah, this is so embarrassing... A few days ago, he said he wanted to come and spend the festival with me, but he started to feel unwell as soon as he arrived last night, and now, he's gone and passed out...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: I think maybe the journey took it out of him, or perhaps he caught a cold on the way... Anyway, I was about to take him to Bubu Pharmacy to see the doctor, so I asked Chef Mao to watch the store while I'm gone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you weren't gonna carry him all that way by yourself, were you? Let us help!

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: I couldn't possibly ask that of you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. Let's just get him to the doctor.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: If you're sure... I'm very grateful for the help.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Why don't I watch the store? As it happens, I know a thing or two about perfume.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I don't believe I've had the pleasure?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! This is Madame Lan Yan, a craftswoman from Chenyu Vale. You can trust her!

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Oh, a friend of yours then. Thank you, Madame Lan Yan, that would be a huge help.

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: Xiangling, I guess that means we're free to head back. Let's get cooking, so the troops can feast on their triumphant return.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, great minds think alike, dad!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Go on, get Timaeus to Bubu Pharmacy. And don't forget to come eat when you're done!

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Thank you all.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, you bring Timaeus to Bubu Pharmacy, where Baizhu takes him to the back room for examination.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You are surprised to see two other familiar faces there...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, it's been a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite, Xingqiu and Chongyun.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Thank you — here's hoping it will be...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean by that? Oh no, did you get sick too?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: No, not me...

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Xingqiu...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: It's alright, these are dear friends. The truth needn't be hidden from them.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: It's... my great-grandfather. A few days ago, he didn't have the strength to get out of bed, and now, he's slipped into a coma.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no! Sorry to hear that. That sounds really serious...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: It's not looking good. We've had several doctors come and see him, but none of them could tell what was wrong, and all left without even writing a prescription.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: None of them could figure out what it was? That seems strange...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: *sigh* Well, he is over a hundred years old now. It's just... we're struggling to come to terms with it.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Our butler came to see me a few days ago, insisting that great-grandfather has been cursed. He urged me to get an exorcist involved.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: So... I went to take a look, and inside His Lordship's room, there was definitely a strange chill in the air. But I'm confident it's not caused by evil spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Well... this is just a theory, but I think that...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: It's fine. You can say.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: It's... fetor of death. A sign that death is near.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... Xingqiu, this must be so hard for you.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Thank you. I'll be okay. Honestly, my father and grandfather are the hardest hit by it... But, we're as prepared as we can be under the circumstances.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I believe my brother's already contacted the funeral parlor, and I'm here to see if Dr. Baizhu can help. My father and grandfather are at home fasting and praying.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Feeling any better?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Much better! I feel fit as a twiddle! I'm sure this is all because I forgot to eat breakfast.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: It's "fit as a fiddle," dear. As in the instrument, not the finger-twitching.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: It's nothing serious, probably just exhaustion from the long journey, then not resting properly afterwards.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: It's all my fault...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I'm prescribing a nutritious soup to be taken every night before bed. Here's the recipe. That should sort him out — but if his symptoms persist, make sure to come and see me again.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Thank you, Dr. Baizhu.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Timaeus is gonna be alright. That's a relief.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Ying'er says you helped bring me here. Thank you ever so much.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't mention it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ying'er, you should probably get this guy back right away. Baizhu says he needs to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Agreed, plus I shouldn't keep Madame Lan Yan waiting too long. Drop by later when you've got a second, so I can thank you both properly.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Dr. Baizhu.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Ah, Master Xingqiu... I won't beat around the bush: The situation is looking a little more complicated than I'd initially thought.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Baizhu wasn't speaking the whole truth just now. Timaeus's situation is exceptionally strange... and strikingly similar to His Lordship's condition!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Wait... So Timaeus has the same illness as my great-grandfather?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: It would appear so, although it's debatable whether it is an "illness," per se... The truth is, they are both aging at an accelerated rate.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: What? Really?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Yes. Significantly faster than the average person. But so far, I have not managed to determine the cause.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Not only does it mystify Baizhu, even I've never witnessed such a malady! Unless, of course, it was so long ago that I have since forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Timaeus is in the prime of his life, so a little extra exhaustion is nothing dangerous. But His Lordship is so advanced in years already...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: That's terrible... So something is... surreptitiously cutting years off their lives?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Cutting years off their lives"!? What a turn of phrase, that sounds horrible...

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: *sigh* Baizhu even tried using the secret art on Timaeus earlier, but it was useless. This is a most stubborn disease.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: There are a few other remedies I can try, even if it's just trial and error at this point. This morning, I sent Qiqi to Mt. Qingce to look for a certain herb. There's still a chance we might turn things around if we're lucky.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Oh, and speaking of Qingce — has His Lordship been there recently, Master Xingqiu?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: To Qingce Village, you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Yes, we visit there every year during Lantern Rite to run a clinic. But this year, before the clinic had even started, they sent someone all the way here to ask for medical advice. The situation seems urgent.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: And then, the patient from Mondstadt who I just saw tells me he stopped off in Qingce Village during his journey... I can't help but wonder if there's some connection.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: If I'm not mistaken, I do believe great-grandfather visited some friends in Qingce Village not too long ago. My father went with him.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Aha. Just as we suspected...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: What is it? I heard the rumors about a god's remains in Qingce... is that what's causing this?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: God's remains? Which one?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Well firstly, I read about this in a book I bought from a street vendor, so it's not the most credible source.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: But the book told of a hidden palace in the Qingce mountain range called the "Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula." It is enchanted with the seven-and-eight-gates method, with which it suppressed countless evil spirits, the most revered of them being a god known as Tao Dou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so... Tao Dou's remains!? That's what's causing this mystery illness?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Not to steal anyone's thunder, but while I do suspect a connection with Qingce Village, I highly doubt that god remains are the cause.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: That's right! The slightest trace of god remains, and Baizhu and I would surely have sensed them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good point... Then what could be the true cause?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Master Xingqiu, I will head to Qingce Village to investigate further after Qiqi returns. Hopefully, I will have more answers after that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we're pros at gathering stuff. Just tell us where to go and we'll track down those herbs, no problem.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Hehe, I am most grateful for the offer. I'll be sure to let you know if I need your assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Thank you for everything, Dr. Baizhu.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Merely doing my duty.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, you take care of yourself too, Baizhu.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Don't worry about me. I am keenly aware of my limits.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, it was good to see you. But now I must return home, and relay Dr. Baizhu's words to my family.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I'll come with you. I wanna take another look at His Lordship's room.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Very well.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Bye, everyone. And don't worry about me, I'm doing fine.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: In all honesty, I've never been as close with my great-grandfather as my father and grandfather. Given his age, he already wasn't speaking much by the time I was around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, come on now. We get that you don't want us to worry, but there's no need to downplay it, alright? We should be supporting you here, not the other way around!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Paimon's a lot smarter than I remember... I guess it's been a long time since we last met.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Paimon's always been smart!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Haha... You know, recently, a phrase that Hu Tao always says has been on my mind a lot: "Live in life, die in death"...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: But she must be exceptionally busy these days, as I've barely seen her at all. So how about we all go for meal together in a few days time, when everything's calmed down?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds great. I'm free whenever.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Then it's decided. See you in a few days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even though Baizhu ruled out god remains as the cause, Paimon still wants to get to the bottom of this Tao Dou business... It's a shame Keqing had to disappear before she could tell us more.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lan Yan seems quite knowledgeable about it too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: True... Then let's head back and ask her. Come on, Xiangling's waiting on us too.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back. Thanks again for helping me get Timaeus to the doctor — please, take this Mora as a small token of our gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You shouldn't have... I barely lifted a finger.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Well that's gotta be an understatement — I doubt you carried me all the way to Bubu Pharmacy by one finger! Honorary Knight, I can't thank you enough. Please, let us give you something for your efforts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks you're misunderstanding what that phrase means, but okay...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: You'll have to excuse him. I think his efforts to learn the local dialect have fried the language part of his brain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, well no more studying for you! Go get some rest, doctor's orders! And if you take a turn for the worse, get back to Bubu Pharmacy right away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: By the way, where did Lan Yan go?

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Ah yes, I almost forgot to mention — she said she went to catch up with Director Hu. She told me to pass on the message.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so she left?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Ying'er, I'd like three— Oh! What's this? Is Scent of Spring under new management?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Haha, perish the thought! Ms. Ying'er had to run an errand, so I'm just watching the shop until she gets back.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Aha, I see. Well, Miss Temporary-New-Management, could I trouble you for three boxes of Red Dust Under Rolling Clouds?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Red Dust Under Rolling Clouds... I think that rings a bell. Not a scent the average young lady would choose though.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Correct. So you probably won't find it on the shelves. More likely hidden in a corner at the back somewhere. Would you mind digging it out?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Not at all. One moment...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Here, is this what you're looking for? If I'm not mistaken, it's used exclusively for ritual purposes.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh? A lady of culture, I see... That is not common knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Hehe. Let me wrap this up for you.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Wait, wait! I see it now! You're from the Lan lineage of Chenyu Vale, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Huh? How can you tell?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Your hairpiece. It's the Jade-Plumed Silverwing, one of the Three Immortals of Tao Dou. Hehe, am I right, or am I right?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: How did... Sorry, who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hehehe, let's just say I'm a fellow lady of culture. But alas, I'm in a rush today, so I'll have to say goodbye for now.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I hope we meet again soon, Miss Temporary-New-Management.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Grandpa was right, Liyue Harbor is full of hidden talents. I would never have expected the average perfume customer to be so knowledgeable...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Director Hu, I gotta say, that outfit looks really good on you.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Why thank you, Ms. Ying'er. I was just procuring some perfume from your fine establishment. Your temporary replacement provided a magnificent service.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Haha, that's good to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Wait... Director Hu?

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Hey, we're back. Thanks for watching the store, Madame Lan.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Ms. Ying'er, that person you spoke to just now... Who was that?

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Hu Tao. Director Hu Tao, of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Huh? But I thought she wore the funeral parlor uniform with the Harmony Hexagram Hat?

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: I guess she just changed into something more festive for the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Shoot... I was face-to-face with her, and I had no idea...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Sorry, Ms. Ying'er, something's come up. Please let the others know I had to leave.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Huh? What could possibly be so urgent...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then she just ran off after Hu Tao? Weird...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe she'll be at the funeral parlor.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Are you going to look for her? If so, could you take this with you? I just found it in the store.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait... isn't this one of those rattan figures?

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Whatever it is, we don't sell them. So I'm guessing Madame Lan left it here by accident.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, well she definitely makes these. Although, this one's pretty different from the ones she made for the street fair. Plus, it has a sigil on it for some reason...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Not the kind of thing you see every day, that's for sure. It could be important, so if it does belong to Madame Lan, I'd like to get it back to her as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then let's head to Wangsheng Funeral Parlor again. Whatever it's for, the sooner she gets it back, the better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Miss Undertaker. Are Hu Tao and Madame Lan back yet?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Sorry, I'm afraid not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? How strange. They were definitely heading this way... Maybe Hu Tao had another appointment. Any idea where we might find them?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: If it was anything business-related, I expect the director would have let me know. I was aware she had a meeting earlier today, for instance. But she doesn't keep me informed about her private affairs.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you're saying, Hu Tao is dealing with a private matter?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: It's possible. The director seems to have had a lot on her mind lately. In the past, she'd usually show up to work in the mid-morning, but recently she's been getting here before the sun's up. She said she's had trouble sleeping, and has been dreaming more than usual.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Trouble sleeping? ...Are we talking about the same Hu Tao here? That doesn't sound like her at all...

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: You might want to talk to our consultant, Zhongli. He's closer to her than I am.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, good idea! How did we not think of that... So where can we find him? Probably sipping tea somewhere, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Hehe. He's just across the road on the second floor, watching an opera. If you listen carefully, you might be able to hear it...

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Afar
dialogues.text: Through discordant tones and tragic fates...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah! Paimon hears singing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like Zhongli is the only one taking it easy today. Let's go say hi.

talks.objective: Find Zhongli, who is currently listening to opera

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: By the way, I'll be performing The Sanctification of Tao Dou on the day of the Lantern Rite. That's the one I was just practicing earlier. It's only a few days away now... I'd be honored if you could come and support me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that's what you were singing just now? Paimon definitely wants to hear the full thing. We'll be there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were actually learning about the Eight Adepts earlier, but we never found out who the Three Beasts of Tao Dou were.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Oh really? Well for starters, the Three Beasts of Tao Dou are also known as the Three Immortals of Tao Dou.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: They were the Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame, the Jade-Plumed Silverwing, and the Gold-Eyed Celadon Mare. Three auspicious beasts, all with the power to take on human form.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! So they really weren't human, huh... Um, the Lone Butterfly sounds pretty self-explanatory, but what about the silverwing and celadon mare? What kind of creatures were they?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Silverwing was a swallow, and the Celadon Mare was a white horse. Legend holds that after purifying Tao Dou, Silverwing and Wind Reader went wandering together, but the white horse retreated into seclusion.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Have you ever read Moonlit Bamboo Forest? That story mentions a white horse that roamed the Qingce mountain range. A lot of people think she was the Gold-Eyed Celadon Mare.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, cool! So... what about the butterfly? What did they get up to?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: The Lone Butterfly gave her life during the purification spell... She was the only one of the eight to sacrifice herself in this way.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Even though the eight had remarkable powers, purifying a god of Tao Dou's caliber was no mean feat. They had to resort to a secret art called the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Array.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: The method involves obfuscating one of the gates so that evil can't escape. The Lone Butterfly was in charge of the gate that was chosen to be obfuscated, and so she disappeared from the world in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw... That's so tragic...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: But all was not lost. According to the legend, Old Man Wuwang, another one of the eight who looked up to her a lot, took up her mantle and kept her legacy alive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Interesting... And then he taught that to the founders of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, right? Didn't they train under him?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Exactly. That's where it feels like fate came into play. After giving her life to restore order to the realm of the dead, some chance meetings ensured that future generations continued using her methods to guard the border between life and death.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: So although she herself disappeared from the world, her mission to protect Liyue is still alive and well, thousands of years on. Anyway, that's basically the whole story of how the Eight Adepts purified Tao Dou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now we finally have names for the full roster. Thanks, Yun Jin!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: My pleasure. I haven't performed this opera in a long, long time, so I still have a fair bit of brushing up to do before I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't practice too much, or you'll tire your voice out.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Heh, thanks, I appreciate it. See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hey guys! Are you finally done? I've been waiting forever!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, Xiangling! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Tracking you guys down, obviously! You really made me work for it, too.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: It's honestly a little rich that you're out here telling everyone else to take care of themselves and keep a good work-life balance when you are apparently too busy to eat!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Keep this up, and I'll have to drag you to the dinner table and force feed you my delicious cooking against your will!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Here we are, I present to you Chef Xiangling's newest creation: Drunken Plums in Snow. You must be starving, surely? Go on, dig in!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! This is so nice of you, Xiangling. Paimon hadn't noticed how hungry she had gotten, but smelling that food is making Paimon ravenous!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: #Sounds like you have a tough life, hey Paimon? Sometimes you feast, but sometimes {NICKNAME} lets you go hungry. You should ditch {NICKNAME} and hang with me from now on — you'll never go hungry again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Now that is a tempting offer!

choices.text: At least I've never charged you for a single meal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That may be true, but you also pretty much never feed Paimon on time!

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Haha, I was only kidding. I know Paimon loves to eat, but I think it'd take more than food to pry her away from your side.

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Anyway, enough about that — time for you guys to eat. Whatever your plans are after this, they'll go much better on a full stomach!

choices.text: Enjoy watching her eat your whole business into oblivion...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh come on, it's only one extra customer!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Go get yourselves to the fair. I'll join you as soon as I can.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Something else I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the god remains in Mt. Qingce...

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Still musing about that, hmm... I suppose you're remembering the events with Jiangli and Jialiang from last time? It did cross our minds as well.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: At the time, we assumed the god remains in question were the chi blood, but hearing what Master Xingqiu had to say has us second guessing ourselves. Perhaps it wasn't the chi after all, but Tao Dou...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Either way, there's no trace of any god remains on His Lordship or Timaeus. There has to be another explanation for their symptoms.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Yes. We'll just have to wait until Qiqi comes back.

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: What's on the menu, Xiangling?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I'm thinking, my latest creation! You know the one: Drunken Plums in Snow!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: ...Swallows will return for a new nest!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Remarkable, Ms. Yun. You have breathed fresh life into an old classic and, I daresay, surpassed the original.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: You flatter me, Mr. Zhongli. I'm just glad my voice held out — I'm a little out of practice...

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Nonsense, Sir Yun! You were as stunning as ever. And if that was you out of practice, well! The official Lantern Rite performance is sure to be truly sensational.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Zhongli, hey Yun Jin! How's it going?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: #Wow, {NICKNAME} and Paimon! What a lovely surprise!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It's been too long, old friends. Are you here for the opera?

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Oh dear, what a pity. I'm afraid you just missed today's performance... and Ms. Yun needs to rest her voice now, or she'll strain it.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's okay, Tea Master Liu — these two are good friends of mine. If they'd like to hear me sing, a few more minutes won't do me any harm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, thanks Yun Jin! But hopefully you don't think we came here just to show up late and demand a private performance...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Oh, of course not, heh... I'm guessing you're here for Mr. Zhongli, then?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Oh? And how might I be of assistance?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, so... A friend of ours left something behind at a shop, we're trying to return it to her, and all we know is she's probably with Hu Tao. Any idea where Hu Tao might be?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The Director is a free spirit who roams far and wide. She could be most anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, great... Well this is just fantastic...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Is it something important? The thing she left behind, I mean.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the thing — we don't know what it's for. But we wanna get it back to her as soon as possible, just in case she really needs it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Show the rattan figure)

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Oh, goodness! THAT'S what you're trying to get back to her? But isn't that... a Pentad Rattan!?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Pentad Rattan...? So you recognize this?

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Haven't you heard? The word on the street is that the patriarch of the Feiyun Commerce Guild has fallen gravely ill. They say his family found an ominous-looking rattan figure in his bedroom... and there was a Pentad Fortune Conveyance talisman on it.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: That cursed thing must have been put there to steal his good fortune... it's destroying his health, wealth, and every other good thing in his life!

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: And based on the description, your rattan figure looks suspiciously similar. It could even be the same one that... Ugh, get it away from me, I don't want that thing anywhere near me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Relax, it's fine! This one definitely belongs to Madame Lan. Besides, we've had it on us this whole time, and nothing bad's happened to us yet!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Madame Lan? You mean, from the Chenyu Vale Artisans Association?

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Oh, now that would explain a lot! The Lans of Chenyu Vale practice Qimen magic... This Pentad Fortune Conveyance business would be right up their alley!

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: This leaves only one question unanswered. Namely... Why would the Lans of Chenyu Vale have a bone to pick with the Feiyun Commerce Guild?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Uh, what? Will you listen to yourself? You can't seriously believe all that. You'd sooner convince Paimon that Rex Lapis was a slime...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Heh, the latter is certainly the more compelling theory. Master Liu, you appear to have been misinformed by these rumors, and also failed to notice the Guyan Sigil on this particular rattan figure.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Oh? Please enlighten me, Mr. Zhongli.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This is the Sign of Vaisravana, one of the four main exorcism sigils. A most upstanding and auspicious sign, by no means cursed.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: As a matter of fact, a series of Fortune Coins bearing the exorcism sigils recently entered circulation in Liyue Harbor. I am somewhat surprised that you didn't recognize it, Master Liu.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Oh! ...Yes, yes, of course, I remember now. Thank you for jogging my memory, Mr. Zhongli! I am humbled by your superior erudition.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This makes way more sense than Madame Lan going around trying to curse people to death.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: I guess the rattan figure they found in His Lordship's room must have been put there by someone in his family to bring good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, there's a good chance Madame Lan also purposely left this behind to keep Timaeus safe and well.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: In all likelihood, yes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew! Guess we don't need to find her so urgently after all. We were just worried that losing this might've ruined her plans.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But that said... What did she need Hu Tao for, anyway? And what is Hu Tao up to that's keeping her so busy? Paimon has a bad feeling about it for some reason...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Any ideas, Zhongli?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The director's mind is a labyrinth I could not hope to comprehend. She probably has more things she has to think about than the rest of us combined.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are any of those thoughts the kind that might keep someone up at night?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: She has never mentioned that.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: But as the director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, she has a solemn duty to balance the forces of life and death in Liyue. I would be surprised, and even a little unsettled, if she were truly as carefree as she appears.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: I agree. I've known Hu Tao for a while now, and for all her eccentricities, she takes pride in what she does. As her friends, we should just be there for her when she needs us.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed. The director's competence is the only reason I can afford to sit here enjoying a fine cup of tea and listening to the opera.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... having a competent boss isn't an excuse to slack off, you know!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Haha, I think Mr. Zhongli just means you should have faith in Hu Tao. There's no need to worry about her so much.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fair point... Heh, somehow, seeing how calm Zhongli is about the whole thing does make Paimon feel much more at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You two ought to be out enjoying the festivities. The Lantern Rite only comes once a year, so make the most of it.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: ...If you're still worried, take this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: A Fortune Coin. It has recently become customary to give them as gifts, so in the spirit of the season, this is my gift to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Zhongli actually left the house with cash!? Now THIS is a Lantern Rite to remember!

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Goodness gracious! Mr. Zhongli, that looks like a very special coin you have there! Is that... one of the fabled Rex Coins!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ..."Rex Coin"!?

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Yes, look at the design on the face — it's quite different from the typical coins you see in circulation. It appears to be a symbol of Rex Lapis... There's no doubt about it: This is a Rex Coin, which means it once passed through the hands of the Lord of Geo himself!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This is simply a curio I picked up from a street vendor, Master Liu. Almost certainly a replica. But I can introduce you to the vendor if you are interested.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Oh... So it's just a souvenir, then? I assumed it was a family heirloom of great value.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #Haha. {NICKNAME}, please take this. May it bring you comfort when your mind is troubled.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So it's an anti-anxiety coin? How is that supposed to work?

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Aha, well, even if the coin itself is a replica, the symbol of Rex Lapis is still genuine. And if the symbol is real, so are its effects! So long as you have this coin, Rex Lapis will always be with you.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Mr. Zhongli, would you mind showing me to the vendor from whom you acquired this coin? I wouldn't mind procuring a little of the Lord of Geo's good fortune for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Very well. The walk will do me good. Friends, may we meet again soon.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: You are gonna concentrate on resting and recovering for the next few days, you hear?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Yes, Ma'am! What the lady wants, the lady gets.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Hehe, now there's a turn of phrase I could get used to.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: So, Mr. Zhongli, where exactly is this vendor's stall?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Gone, it seems. Perhaps they sold all their stock and moved on.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: ...You're not making this all up, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I wouldn't dream of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What're all these Mora for? They're huge! And so shiny.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Lady Yuheng said they're Fortune Coins. Go on, give them a rub, it'll bring you good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are these lanterns?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Nope! They're toys that shoot fireworks! New to this year's festival. You should try them, Paimon.
